name: Polish & Release Prep
one_line_goal: Make it look finished, make it legal to publish, and produce a signed build that installs and works.
objective: Final UX polish, branding, privacy policy, store compliance material, signed release build and documentation for future maintenance.
rationale: A correct app that looks unfinished will not be trusted with someone's savings, and a correct app without a privacy policy cannot be published at all. Both are release blockers, so both belong here rather than in a hopeful backlog.
entry_criteria: No open Sev-1 or Sev-2 defects.
Privacy verification passed on a release-configuration build.

how_to_work_this_stage.unit_of_work: One substage per working session. Work them strictly in listed order; do not parallelise or skip.
how_to_work_this_stage.between_substages: Tick the substage off, append evidence to docs/reports/STAGE_10_WORKLOG.md, then start the next. No user approval needed between substages.
how_to_work_this_stage.at_stage_end: The final substage assembles the stage report and stops for user approval before the next stage file is opened.
substage_list: 10.2 State polish and debug affordance removal
10.4 Store compliance, data safety and OAuth verification
10.6 Code shrinking and release-build smoke test

substages.name: Branding and visual identity
substages.goal: Produce the app icon, splash screen and finalised theming that make a finance app feel safe to use.
substages.why_it_matters: First impressions decide whether someone trusts an app with their savings.
entry_criteria: No open Sev-1 or Sev-2 defects.
Privacy verification passed on a release-configuration build.

work.action: Design the app icon, including the Android adaptive icon with properly separated foreground and background layers.
details: Check it against circular, squircle and rounded-square launcher masks.
Check it at the smallest launcher size, where detail disappears.
Check it against both light and dark system themes.

work.action: Design the splash screen using the platform's native splash mechanism.
details: The native mechanism avoids the blank frame that a Flutter-drawn splash cannot.

work.action: Finalise light and dark themes and remove every remaining hardcoded colour, spacing or font literal.
details: Run a search to prove none remain rather than assuming.

work.action: Confirm the business scope's visual distinction is intentional and consistent, and still works in dark mode and greyscale.
Verify icon and splash on the smallest and largest supported screen densities.
Verify the app name as displayed on the launcher, which is often truncated and rarely checked.

acceptance_criteria: The adaptive icon renders correctly in circular, squircle and rounded-square launchers.
There is no blank or white flash between the splash and the first screen.
A search finds no colour or spacing literal outside the theme definition.
The launcher name displays correctly without awkward truncation.
must_not: Do not ship a placeholder icon.
common_pitfalls: An adaptive icon whose foreground is clipped by the launcher mask.
A Flutter-drawn splash that appears after a blank frame, which reads as a slow app.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: State polish and debug affordance removal
substages.goal: Bring every empty, error and loading state to a finished standard, and remove everything that should not ship.
substages.why_it_matters: Half-finished states are where an app stops feeling trustworthy, and a leftover developer menu is where it stops looking professional.
entry_criteria: Substage 10.1 (Branding and visual identity) is complete and ticked off.
inputs: The developer route menu added in substage 3.7.

work.action: Review every empty state: does it explain what will appear here and offer the single most useful next action?
Review every error state: plain language, an actionable cause, and a route forward.
details: No stack traces. No bare error codes. No provider jargon.
Every message should tell the user what to do next, not only what went wrong.

work.action: Review every loading state: skeletons or inline indicators rather than full-screen blocking spinners.
details: Nothing may block on the network.

work.action: Add transitions and micro-interactions that aid comprehension, particularly when money moves between categories during a redirect.
details: Respect the reduced-motion system setting.

work.action: Add haptic feedback for confirmation of destructive and money-moving actions, respecting system settings.
Ensure every destructive action has a confirmation and, where feasible, an undo.
Remove the developer route menu, all debug logging, any test fixture shipped in assets, and any hidden debug gesture.
details: Verify by inspecting the built artefact, not only the source.

work.action: Verify the release build contains no leftover TODO-visible text, placeholder copy or lorem ipsum.

acceptance_criteria: No screen shows a raw exception message anywhere.
Every empty state names a next action.
The developer menu and all debug affordances are absent from the release build, verified by inspecting the artefact.
No placeholder copy remains anywhere in the app.
Reduced-motion and haptic system settings are respected.
must_not: Do not leave a debug entry point behind a hidden gesture.
Do not show a technical error message to a user.
common_pitfalls: A debug menu removed from navigation but still reachable by route name.
Animation that ignores the reduced-motion setting and makes the app unusable for some users.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Privacy policy drafting and publication
substages.goal: Turn the verified privacy behaviour into a published, accurate, plain-language policy.
substages.why_it_matters: R-04. It is a hard blocker for publication, it is the public statement of the product's core promise, and it always takes longer than expected.
entry_criteria: Substage 10.2 (State polish and debug affordance removal) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Draft the policy from PRIVACY_SOURCE.md, covering every required point.
details: What data the app collects and what it does not.
That financial data is stored only on the device and in the user's own Google account.
Exactly which OAuth scopes are requested and why each one is needed.
That the developer cannot read the data.
That there are no third-party recipients, no analytics and no advertising.
How the user deletes their data, locally and remotely, with concrete steps.
How to contact the developer, and the effective date.

work.action: Write it in plain language a non-lawyer can follow.
details: Every claim must correspond to verified behaviour from Stage 9, not to intention.

work.action: Note clearly that this is drafting support and not legal advice, and that a qualified person should review it before publication.
Publish it at a stable public URL.
details: Both the store listing and the OAuth consent screen require one, and the URL must not change later.

work.action: Link to it from within the app, and verify the in-app link opens the published version.
Cross-check every statement in the policy against the Stage 9 traffic capture and permission list.
details: A policy that overstates or understates behaviour is a compliance problem, in either direction.

acceptance_criteria: The policy is live at a stable URL and covers every required point.
Every claim corresponds to verified Stage 9 behaviour.
The in-app link opens the published policy.
The need for qualified legal review is stated explicitly to the user.
must_not: Do not copy a template policy that describes behaviour this app does not have.
Do not present the draft as legal advice.
common_pitfalls: A policy claiming no data is collected while the app requests a profile scope.
A policy URL that later moves, breaking both the store listing and the consent screen.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Store compliance, data safety and OAuth verification
substages.goal: Prepare every artefact the store and the OAuth consent process require, matching actual behaviour.
substages.why_it_matters: R-04. These are hard blockers, and OAuth verification in particular can take weeks of calendar time.
entry_criteria: Substage 10.3 (Privacy policy drafting and publication) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Complete the Play Console data safety declaration.
details: Every answer must match verified behaviour, checked against the Stage 9 traffic capture.
A mismatch is a common cause of rejection and of later enforcement action.

work.action: Prepare the OAuth consent screen content and begin verification if the current requirements call for it.
details: Check the current requirements in official documentation rather than assuming; scope classifications change.
Record the expected wait time and treat it as a scheduling dependency, not a formality.

work.action: Prepare the store listing assets.
details: Title, short description and full description that describe only what the app actually does.
Feature graphic, and at least four screenshots: onboarding, income split with a visible redirect, the dashboard, and a report.
Content rating questionnaire response.

work.action: Confirm the listing makes no claim the app does not deliver.
details: In particular, nothing that implies bank connectivity, financial advice or guaranteed outcomes.
This is both a rejection risk and a trust risk.

work.action: Confirm the target SDK level meets the current Play requirement at the time of upload.
Prepare the release notes for version 1.0.0 from the Stage 9 findings, including the known limitations.
Record the verification status and any expected wait in the release checklist so it is visible.

acceptance_criteria: Every data safety answer is verifiable against Stage 9 evidence.
The store listing makes no claim the app does not deliver.
OAuth verification has been started if required, with its status and expected wait recorded.
Target SDK meets the current Play requirement.
Release notes and known limitations are written and honest.
must_not: Do not answer a data safety question optimistically.
Do not imply bank connectivity or financial advice anywhere in the listing.
common_pitfalls: Starting OAuth verification the week of launch and discovering it takes weeks.
Screenshots from a debug build showing the developer menu.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Signing and build configuration
substages.goal: Configure release signing safely and produce the signed artefacts.
substages.why_it_matters: A lost or committed signing key permanently ends the ability to update the app under that listing.
entry_criteria: Substage 10.4 (Store compliance, data safety and OAuth verification) is complete and ticked off.
inputs: The OAuth client configuration from Stage 7.

work.action: Generate the upload keystore and store it securely outside the repository.
details: Document where it is stored and the recovery plan, without recording the secret itself anywhere in the repository.
Losing this key without Play App Signing enabled means the app can never be updated.

work.action: Configure release signing so no key material or password is ever committed.
details: Use a gitignored properties file or environment variables.
Verify the repository history contains no secret, not only the current tree.

work.action: Enable Play App Signing so a lost upload key is recoverable.
Verify the release build against the registered OAuth fingerprint.
details: Debug and release fingerprints differ; sign-in fails silently if the release fingerprint was never registered.
This was prepared in Stage 7; confirm it here on the actual release build.

work.action: Set the version name and version code, and define the versioning scheme for future releases.
Build the App Bundle and also a signed APK for direct sideload testing.
Record the exact build commands so the build is reproducible from a clean checkout.
Record the artefact size.

acceptance_criteria: The signed App Bundle builds reproducibly from a clean checkout, with the command recorded.
No secret, keystore or password is present anywhere in the repository or its history.
Play App Signing is enabled.
The release build's fingerprint is registered with the OAuth client.
Version name and code are set and the scheme is documented.
must_not: Do not commit the keystore or any password.
Do not rely on the debug fingerprint for release sign-in.
common_pitfalls: A keystore committed once and removed later, which leaves it in git history forever.
Discovering at first release test that sign-in fails because only the debug fingerprint was registered.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Code shrinking and release-build smoke test
substages.goal: Enable shrinking safely and prove the release build behaves identically to the debug build.
substages.why_it_matters: Shrinking strips reflection-based code, and database, JSON and Google libraries are the usual casualties - always discovered at the worst moment.
entry_criteria: Substage 10.5 (Signing and build configuration) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Enable code shrinking and resource shrinking.
Add the keep rules the chosen libraries require, and verify each rather than assuming.
details: Database serialisation, JSON serialisation and the Google client libraries are the usual candidates.

work.action: Install the release build on a clean device and run the full manual checklist from Stage 9 against it.
details: Against the release build specifically, not a debug build.
The first database access, the first sync and the first sign-in are the highest-risk moments.

work.action: Run the full automated suite against the release configuration where possible.
Compare release and debug behaviour on the money-critical paths: income split, redirect, override, undo, report and export.
Re-run the money correctness reconciliation script against data produced by the release build.
Record the artefact size before and after shrinking.
If any shrinking-related failure is found, fix the keep rules rather than disabling shrinking, and re-run the whole smoke test.

acceptance_criteria: The release build installs on a clean device and completes the primary journey including sign-in and sync.
The full manual checklist passes against the release build.
Money-critical paths behave identically in release and debug.
The reconciliation script reports zero discrepancies against release-build data.
Artefact size before and after shrinking is recorded.
must_not: Do not disable shrinking to work around a failure.
Do not skip the release-build manual checklist.
common_pitfalls: A stripped serialiser that fails on the first database read, after the store listing is already live.
Testing the release build only on a device that already has app data, hiding first-run failures.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Documentation for future maintenance
substages.goal: Write the documents that let someone extend this app in six months without archaeology.
substages.why_it_matters: That someone is often the same person with no memory of the details.
entry_criteria: Substage 10.6 (Code shrinking and release-build smoke test) is complete and ticked off.
inputs: All documentation produced across Stages 1 to 9.

work.action: Write README.md.
details: What the app is, screenshots, feature summary.
Setup from a clean machine, how to run tests, how to run code generation.
Project structure and the architecture summary, linking to ARCHITECTURE.md, SCHEMA.md, ALLOCATION_ALGORITHM.md and SYNC.md.
A docs index so nothing written across ten stages is orphaned.

work.action: Write the guide to extending the category system.
details: How to add a category type, what the engine assumes about types, which validations must be updated, which tests must be extended.
State explicitly that any change touching allocation requires new golden vectors and a re-run of the property tests.

work.action: Write docs/RELEASE_RUNBOOK.md.
details: Version bump, changelog, full check run, reconciliation script, manual checklist, build, upload, staged rollout, post-release watch, rollback.

work.action: Write docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md covering sign-in failures, sync stalls, migration problems and export or import issues.
Write CONTRIBUTING.md.
details: The invariants that must never be broken - the manifest INV list is the core of it.
Testing expectations per layer, and the commit and branch conventions.

work.action: Write CHANGELOG.md for version 1.0.0 with features and known limitations.
Archive every stage report under docs/reports/ and finalise docs/TRACEABILITY.md.
Verify README.md by following it literally on a clean machine, or as close to clean as available.

acceptance_criteria: A developer can go from a clean machine to a running app using README.md alone, verified by following it literally.
The extension guide is specific enough to add a category type without reading the engine source first.
CONTRIBUTING.md states the invariants explicitly, including integer money and the append-only ledger.
Every stage report is archived and TRACEABILITY.md is complete.
No document produced in Stages 1 to 9 is orphaned from the docs index.
must_not: Do not write a README that assumes prior knowledge of the project.
common_pitfalls: Setup instructions that work only because of local state on the author's machine.
An extension guide that describes the intended design rather than the implemented one.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

substages.name: Release readiness review
substages.goal: Run the final check against the exact artefact that will be published, and decide honestly whether to ship.
substages.why_it_matters: The last chance to catch something that would be embarrassing, or harmful to someone's savings.
entry_criteria: Substage 10.7 (Documentation for future maintenance) is complete and ticked off.

work.action: Re-run the full automated suite and the Stage 9 manual checklist against the exact release artefact.
Re-run the money correctness reconciliation against a fresh multi-year synthetic dataset.
Confirm no debug logging, developer menu, test account or hardcoded fixture survives in the release build, by inspecting the artefact.
Confirm the privacy policy URL in the app matches the published one and opens correctly.
Confirm the app works fully offline on a device that has never had network access.
details: This is the final proof of NFR-02, on the artefact that will actually ship.

work.action: Finalise release notes and the known limitations list from the Stage 9 findings.
Plan the staged rollout and define what would trigger a halt or a rollback.
details: Define the specific signals: crash rate, sign-in failure reports, any report of an incorrect balance.

work.action: Define post-release monitoring.
details: With no analytics, the only feedback channel is user reports, so make contacting the developer easy from within the app.
State plainly that this is a deliberate trade-off of the privacy design, and what it means operationally.

work.action: Write docs/reports/STAGE_10_REPORT.md and prepare the final gate question.

acceptance_criteria: The full suite passes against the release artefact, not a debug build.
The reconciliation script reports zero discrepancies.
A clean-device offline install completes the primary journey.
The in-app privacy policy link opens the published policy.
Release notes and known limitations are written and honest.
Rollback triggers are defined specifically, not vaguely.
must_not: Do not publish with a known Sev-1 or Sev-2 defect.
Do not add analytics at the last minute to monitor the launch.
common_pitfalls: Final verification run against a build that is not the one uploaded.
No defined rollback trigger, so a bad release runs on judgement in the moment.
definition_of_done: Every acceptance criterion above is demonstrably met, with evidence recorded.

checkpoint.action: Final substage. Assemble the stage report, then STOP and request approval using approval_gate.question_to_user below.
escalate_immediately_if: Any discrepancy in the reconciliation run, or any Sev-1 or Sev-2 defect discovered during final review.

stage_deliverables.path: Signed release App Bundle and APK

stage_definition_of_done: A signed App Bundle exists, installs on a clean device, and completes the primary journey including sign-in and sync.
The privacy policy is published and accurate.
The Play data safety declaration matches verified behaviour.
README.md takes a developer from clean machine to running app.
No debug affordance, secret or placeholder survives in the release build.
The full automated suite and the manual checklist pass against the release artefact.
TRACEABILITY.md is complete and every stage report is archived.
stage_must_not: Do not commit the keystore, its password, or any OAuth secret to the repository, in the working tree or in history.
Do not enable code shrinking without a full release-build smoke test.
Do not publish a privacy policy that describes behaviour the app does not have.
Do not add analytics or crash reporting at the last minute to monitor the launch.
Do not ship with a known Sev-1 or Sev-2 defect.
Do not leave the developer route menu, debug logging or test fixtures in the release build.
Do not present the drafted privacy policy as legal advice.
anti_patterns: Treating the privacy policy as a formality to copy from a template, when it is the public statement of the product's core promise.
Testing only the debug build and discovering at upload time that release signing breaks sign-in.
Enabling shrinking on the last day and shipping a build that crashes on first database access.
A README that assumes the reader already knows the project.

artifacts_next_stage_consumes: There is no next stage. The release runbook and manual checklist become the process for every future version.
The open questions register and deferred features from Stage 1 become the version 1.1 backlog.
handoff.summary_to_write: State what shipped, what was deferred, what the user should know before relying on the app for real money, and what the next release should contain.

approval_gate.question_to_user: Stage 10 (Release prep) is complete. A signed App Bundle is built and verified on a clean device, the privacy policy is published, and documentation is complete. Known limitations: <list>. Deferred to v1.1: <list>. Ready to publish?
